result.title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
result.comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Extended version of a paper submitted for publication
result.summary: This paper studies the problem of safe tool execution for large language model (LLM) agents under prompt injection. Using Petri nets, we formalize the execution harness between the LLM and its tools as a supervisory control problem, in which marks represent capabilities, approvals and budgets. Since a transition fires only if the marks it needs are present, an injected request whose preconditions are unmet or already spent is refused regardless of its wording. Treating tool outcomes as uncontrollable, we enforce safety by the conventional maximally permissive supervisor, and this safety transfers to the running system under four assumptions. Moreover, to capture an agent that may propose again after a refusal, we introduce the notion of a replanning closed loop, in which each retry costs an inference call. We show that, in this loop, the conventional supervisor can be arbitrarily more intrusive than a stricter safe one. Furthermore, for a given proposer model, the maximally permissive least-intrusive supervisor is characterized as a value-threshold refinement of the conventional one. Under precise conditions, this refinement orders two concurrent actions by at most one monitor place. On an autonomous release agent, we find by synthesis that safe deployment requires a step that the supervisor can refuse after a rollout starts.

AI.brief_summary: 本文将 LLM agent 与其工具之间的执行环节形式化为 Petri 网监督控制问题，以 mark 表示能力、审批与预算，并分析「拒绝后重规划」闭环中传统最大许可监督器的侵入性，进而给出以价值阈值为基础的最小侵入修正。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及视觉或 latent 推理，但其对「推理—行动」切换的前置条件门控、预算消耗与重试成本（每次重试即一次推理调用）的建模，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/STOP 的收益—成本核算与停止准则提供形式化线索，可供核查。
